protocol: sparkDash 3e6d4ef: temperature 0, top_p 1, thinking off, output pinned to 400 tokens with min_tokens + ignore_eos. decode tok/s = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token), the same formula bench/bench.py uses.
why: Under the repository's own protocol (temperature 0.7, thinking on, natural length) the same cell swings 2x on this model, because MTP acceptance is content-dependent. Pinning the text and the length gets the spread to a few percent, which is what makes a build comparison mean anything.
discipline: discard the first measurement set after a start: it is still warming up
checkpoint: heretic-2 W4A16 + the same FP8 PLE on both images

note: one variable at a time, 12 reps each, 0 stalls

steps.label: A  TP2+EP, k=4, nbt4096, seqs12, FULL_DECODE_ONLY
E  full AlexBrandes: + PP2, seqs 8, nbt 2048

conclusion: nvfp4 and k=5 account for all of it. PP2, max-num-seqs 8, max-num-batched-tokens 2048 and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE contribute nothing measurable here.

topic: QSA ring capacity bounds the block size
detail: qsa_indexer.py (upstream) / qsa_cache.py (this image) computes capacity = round_up(compress_ratio + num_speculative_tokens, compress_ratio) and asserts block_size % capacity == 0. compress_ratio is 4, so k<=4 gives capacity 8 and the default attention block size 1616 divides it; k=5 gives capacity 12, which 1616 does not divide. k>=5 therefore needs --block-size 1680 (1680/12 = 140). The failure is a startup AssertionError, not a slow path.

On this checkpoint acceptance is 4.86-5.49 on code and only 2.2-2.9 on prose, so a longer draft wins on code and loses elsewhere. upstream k=4 -> k=5: code +4.4%, ja-prose -4.5%, en-prose -4.3%, ja-list -9.5%. Keep k=4 for mixed traffic.

topic: the stall phenomenon is transient, not steady-state
detail: Earlier in this investigation the same cell swung 2x. With the sampling pinned, 40 consecutive requests straight after a restart ran 225.7-240.1 tok/s with zero stalls. The spread concentrates in the first ~20-70 requests after a start and does not come back: 4-way bursts, a 20k-character prefill, thinking-on requests, 1200-token generations and 0-90s idle gaps all failed to trigger it again. Ten candidate causes were measured and eliminated (power cap, swap, major page faults, PLE gather, preemption, acceptance variance, prefix caching, CUDA-graph misses, TP/EP all-to-all, disk I/O). Unexplained, and recorded as such.

note: upstream reads PLE rows per step with preadv instead of holding the 47 GiB table
